Could it be that they were sending their reports to other units but not to the 3rd Corps? And I'm specifically referring to operations going from July to September of 1995. Would it be possible that they would have sent their reports to a division, a different division, that would have sent you the reports in turn? Maybe you did not see their reports, the detachment reports, for that particular reason? I'm just wondering. Could it be the case?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: As duty operations officer in the Command of the 3rd Corps, I received reports from subordinate units, and from among others, there were reports from the 35th Division and some other divisions. None of these units mentioned in their report the El Mujahedin Detachment, and that's why I don't know anything about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising from the Judge's questions, Mr. Menon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If the witness could now be shown Exhibit 394. And if he could go to page 4 of the B/C/S and page 5 of the English. And actually it's the -- I neglected to mention, but it's the second translation in e-court, the second English translation that I want to bring up, so it should be marked as 0185-5153-2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm getting confused. When you say "the second translations of Exhibit 394", are you suggesting that two translations have been admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Well, they are two duplicates. One is a shorter range and one is a longer range. They are both partial translations of the B/C/S version, it's just that one is more comprehensive than the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, let's see it then and see what happens. Further re-examination by Mr. Menon:

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Mr. Sivro, I'd like to refer you to entry number 19. Did you make that entry?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And from whom are you receiving the information noted in entry number 19?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: From someone who introduced himself as the El Mujahedin Detachment, being from that detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And that entry is -- the time of that entry, 6.20 a.m., if we could just go to the previous page. That would be page 3 of the B/C/S and page 4 of the English. And would you agree with me, Mr. Sivro, that that's dated the 10th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Mr. Sivro, would you agree with me that that's dated the 10th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now if we could go back to page 4 of the B/C/S and page 5 of the English. Mr. Sivro, I refer you to entry number 21, and on the English it continues on to page 6. Mr. Sivro, from whom did you get the information contained in entry number 21? And if we could go to page 6 of the English and we can see the continuation of that. Mr. Sivro, from whom did you get the information set out in entry number 21?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: I received the information from an officer from the Staff, and I can't recall who it was from. Probably someone from the Staff who was dealing with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And who contacted the person at the Staff?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Did you not write here: "Aiman called the 3rd Corps commander"?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: I wrote it that way: "Aiman called the commander of the 3rd Corps and reported that the El Mujahedin Detachment seized the facilities Paljenik and Ravno Ivlje. And it was someone who called me, relayed that information to me, and that's how I put it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, Mr. Sivro, and the time of that is 6.34? If we could move on to page 5 of the B/C/S and page 6 of the English. We're actually on page 6, so if we could stay on that page. And I refer you to entry number 25, Mr. Sivro. The time of that is 7.12.

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: I don't understand. Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: It's entry number 25, Mr. Sivro. In that entry, where is the -- the information that's set out in that entry, where does that originate from?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: At the time, I was at the commander's observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But how was that -- I'm sorry, go ahead, continue.

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: I was at the observation post of the commander, and I wrote down what was going on. Somebody -- some of the officers entered and said that this was what transpired, and I wrote it down. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: But the information, how is it acquired by the 3rd Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Corps was reported to by someone from the Staff. I'm -- someone who I'm writing about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Does it not say the El Mujahedin Detachment informed the commander?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wrote. However, as far as I know, the commander was in my immediate vicinity, or rather I was immediately close to him, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Can you repeat the last part of your answer, Mr. Sivro?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: I was at the observation post, together with the commander, and I did not hear anybody calling from the El Mujahedin Detachment. It must have been someone from the Communications Service who reported this, and this is how I wrote down. Matters unfolded so quickly that I did not really pay that much attention to what I was writing down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: If we could move on to page -- well, stay on page 5 of the B/C/S and move on to page 7 of the English. And I refer you to entry number 29, Mr. Sivro.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: How is the -- how is the 3rd Corps Command obtaining the information in that particular entry?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: Well, probably either from the neighbouring units or this someone Aiman must have called again and given this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You made this entry, did you not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go to page 6 of the B/C/S and page 8 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And I refer you to entry number 35, Mr. Sivro. How is the 3rd Corps obtaining the information set out in that entry?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no idea. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Did you not produce this entry?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: Well, I did, I wrote it, but it wasn't down to me to check up on the information or to go off to persons to see what this was about. I was -- I wrote whatever I was ordered to write, either by my superiors or my colleagues, officers who were engaged in communications. I was engaged in writing this down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And what you wrote down says: "El Mujahedin Detachment reported that the detachment forces had joined at the bridge over the Krivaja River," does it not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: "El Mujahedin Detachment reported that the detachment forces had joined at the bridge over the Krivaja River right before the entrance to the village of Stog."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you going to be much longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'm actually finished, Your Honour, I'm done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will only have one question for the witness. Can we have D445 shown to the witness. Further cross-examination by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Before that, let us clarify this, Witness. You were a person who wrote down a piece of information that you heard from someone; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: In other words, you don't know in what way the information reached that person?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: I was not out in the field. I was at the IKM, at the observation post, and I made note of whatever was said to me by some of the officers or someone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the witness look at page 2 of the document. This is an excerpt from the same operations logbook. Can we turn to page 2 in the English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Mr. Sivro, can you look at entry number 70 for the 12th of May?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: Can you please zoom in on this bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: That's all right. It says: "Aiman, commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment, sought the commander of the 3rd Corps via communications links." Is it right that you wrote this, Mr. Sivro?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wrote. That's -- he introduced himself. I don't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: You know so well, you're so familiar with the El Mujahedin Detachment that you know that this Aiman is a commander?

utterances.speaker: SAFET SIVRO
utterances.text: Well, he introduced himself as the commander. Whether he was a commander or not is something I don't know. He -- anybody could have introduced himself as the commander of the unit, anyone who I didn't know, and I would have written it down that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The record doesn't seem to reflect what we were discussing at all. Something's wrong with the transcript. I believe everything is fine now. I couldn't see any of this on my screen, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you done with your questioning?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a problem with the transcript, page 94, line 25. I said -- or rather I did not say "regarding operations from July to September," I said "operations from July and from September of 1995." Thank you for correcting the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. Mr. Sivro, thank you so much for coming to testify. This brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. We understand that you have taken time off to come and -- yes, madam.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, document D445, can that be given an exhibit number before we finish? Yes, if possible, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Document D445 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 524.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Sivro, thank you very much. I was still saying that this brings us to the conclusion of your testimony, and we just want to thank you for having come to testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused, you may stand down, and please have a pleasant journey back home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And may I just say thank you to the interpreters and other people for staying beyond the time. I'm sorry, we were challenged to complete this witness. Court will adjourn, and we'll reconvene in Courtroom II tomorrow afternoon at quarter past 2.00. Court adjourned.
